quest.title: Witch's Revelation: Special Blend's Instruction
quest.description: You encounter Diona at Barbeloth's fortune-telling booth...
quest.rewards_formatted: Mora x20000, Guide to Freedom x3

dialogues.speaker: Diona
dialogues.text: ...So you can't help me fix this annoying affliction either?

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: Precisely. It's already too deeply intertwined with your fate. Imagine your destiny is a tree — this "affliction" is like a new shoot growing from its branches.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: It's been helping you absorb sunlight and dew this whole time. It long ago began to shape your fate.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: If you cut it off now, the wound left behind might fester, infecting the entire tree.

dialogues.speaker: Diona
dialogues.text: Hmph... You make it sound like it's a good thing. It's clearly getting in my way, keeping me from mixing the drinks I need!

dialogues.speaker: Diona
dialogues.text: It's more like one of those vines that wrap around the trunks of giant trees — restricting their growth and slowly strangling them!

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: Well, if that were the case, your fate would have rejected it, and we could have easily pruned it away... Unfortunately for you, it's not at all what you say it is.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: Alright, enough talk. That should be enough to convince you I'm a legitimate fortune teller, yes?

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: Now, just like I told you, come here and pick a card at random, and let me give you a little advice about your future.

dialogues.speaker: Diona
dialogues.text: Hmm... So, I just pick one at random, hm? Okay... How about this one...? No, wait, this one...!

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: Don't overthink it — no matter how you choose, you can only ever draw the card that's destined for you. Hahahaha...

dialogues.speaker: Diona
dialogues.text: (*shudder*... This fortune teller's laugh is so creepy! She's just like an old witch from a fairy tale!)

dialogues.speaker: Diona
dialogues.text: (But since she's so good at it, her advice could prove really helpful... I have to choose my card carefully!)

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: #Huh? {NICKNAME}, Paimon?

response.speaker: Barbeloth
response.text: True to form, here you are at just the right moment.

response.speaker: Barbeloth
response.text: Hahaha, well said. Compared to an intangible thing like Fate, commissions have a far more intuitive effect on shaping our words and deeds.

response.speaker: Barbeloth
response.text: Now, seeing as you're here, perhaps you could have a word with this little one? She doesn't seem very trusting of an old "witch" like me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, it's not so easy to trust a weird-looking fortune teller who's set up stall in the middle of nowhere...

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: #({NICKNAME} seems to know this fortune teller pretty well? Great, I can finally ask someone I trust...!)

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: #...{NICKNAME}, Paimon, come over here a second. I need to talk to you in private.

choices.text: I was just about to ask...

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: Looking for new ingredients, of course! Hmph, my previous approach to mixing drinks was far too narrow-minded... I kept limiting myself to actual food...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhm... Haha... Paimon wouldn't exactly call the things you put in your drinks "food," Diona...

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: Weeeell, it's all technically edible! As long as you grit your teeth and close your eyes, it's stuff you can force yourself to swallow.

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: Exactly! ...I've already found a bunch of rusted screws, scrapped cables, coagulated chunks of grease, dustbunnies, toejam...

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: And it's all thanks to that guy from the Fontaine Research Institute who makes Fonta. He's been a real help!

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: Well... I heard that really tasty fizzy drink stuff comes from the Fontaine Research Institute, so I headed over to take a look.

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: When I got there, Mr. Heinry let me try a few bottles of the new Fonta flavors. Completely on the house, haha!

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: Mr. Heinry doesn't smell of alcohol at all! Nope, he just smells like Fonta, sweet and tangy, haha. One sniff and you can tell he's a reliable sort of grown up.

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: Aaaand, he was the one who suggested I come to this stall. He said my affliction is probably beyond the Research Institute's ability to analyze.

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: But he heard that this weird fortune-teller who showed up recently near the Court of Fontaine. Apparently, everyone who's been here says she's crazy accurate!

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: "Maybe if you get your fortune told, you'll learn something about what's causing your affliction. If you grasp the principles behind it, perhaps you can find a cure."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well... Hard to argue with that logic! Guess he didn't end up becoming a researcher at the Fontaine Research Institute for nothing...

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: So, I came here to see the fortune-teller... As soon as I walked over, she stopped me and said there was a strange disturbance surrounding me.

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: Before I could ask, she blurted out all the answers to my questions, but...

response.speaker: Barbeloth
response.text: ...But the scientific logic of the Fontaine Research Institute doesn't directly apply to divination.

response.speaker: Barbeloth
response.text: Even if you understand the principles, it doesn't mean the solution will be easy to come by... Just like I told you.

response.speaker: Barbeloth
response.text: Mysticism isn't built of bearings and bolts, and I can't simply "repair" your fate for you.

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: Are you telling me nothing can be changed? Then what's the point of drawing a card...

response.speaker: Barbeloth
response.text: By drawing a card, you may just find a tiny missing gear to fit into the wheel of fate.

response.speaker: Barbeloth
response.text: It may seem insignificant, but when installed correctly, the tiniest gears can still drive massive mechanisms.

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: #You... you're not just humoring me, are you? {NICKNAME}, what do you think...

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: ...Alright, if you say so, then I'll take one...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Under Barbeloth's watchful gaze, Diona reaches out and slowly draws a Lunar Arcanum...

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: Alright, h—here we go. Looks like it's...

response.speaker: Barbeloth
response.text: ...Oh my, how strange... To think the disturbance surrounding you has grown with such vigor.

response.speaker: Barbeloth
response.text: It's no longer a shoot, but a sturdy branch. How curious...

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: Huh? W—What are you saying? Does... does this mean the drinks I mix will taste even better from now on!?

choices.text: That doesn't sound like a bad thing in itself...

response.speaker: Barbeloth
response.text: If we judge solely by your affliction, that would indeed be the case. Furthermore, the card you drew is the reversed High Priestess.

response.speaker: Barbeloth
response.text: Which means you've been too focused on the illusions before the veil. Which is precisely why you've been unable to pass through it for so long.

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: That doesn't sound like it has anything to do with mixing drinks... I thought this card would tell me what ingredients I need to use...

response.speaker: Barbeloth
response.text: Heh... The Lunar Arcana aren't known for creating recipes — at least not yet.

response.speaker: Barbeloth
response.text: But mixing drinks isn't the only way to find the answers you're looking for.

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: The answer is to teach those old boozehounds a lesson, so they never get drunk and cause trouble again.

response.speaker: Barbeloth
response.text: You're certainly driven. But while your body moves forward, your heart remains stuck.

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: That's not true! I... I hate those weird old drunkards from the bottom of my heart! Especially—

response.speaker: Barbeloth
response.text: Haha, I see. Then... have you talked to the one who fills your heart the most?

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: I... Uhm... H—How did you know I was thinking about one person in particular? I didn't even...

response.speaker: Barbeloth
response.text: Through divination, of course. Hehehe, perhaps you should cast aside your impatience and confused emotions, and tell him how you truly feel.

response.speaker: Barbeloth
response.text: You might find it more effective than trying to mix the most disgusting drinks in the world.

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: ...There's no way he'll listen. Once he's started drinking, he doesn't listen to anyone.

response.speaker: Barbeloth
response.text: Perhaps that was true before. But now, you've found a tiny gear from the wheel of fate. Returned to its rightful place, certain things might undergo... subtle changes.

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: You mean that? B-b-b-but it's just a card...

response.speaker: Barbeloth
response.text: Of course not that! I'm talking about your heart — something which has already begun to change.

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: M—My heart hasn't changed at all! Now... I need to go look for ingredients!

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: ...Uhm, how much is the divination fee? I can pay it in full.

response.speaker: Barbeloth
response.text: Oh my, what a well-mannered child. Much more endearing than that other little brat. But there's no need for a fee. Just consider this a gift from a witch.

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: Th—Thank you. If you ever come to Mondstadt... I can treat you to a drink. I guarantee it'll taste delicious.

response.speaker: Barbeloth
response.text: Mondstadt, you say? Yes... If I get the chance, that might not be such a terrible idea...

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: #And thank you for helping me out, {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #No matter the trouble, Paimon and {NICKNAME} will swoop in and save the day!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But swooping in is thirsty work, hehehe... So once we're done, we wouldn't say no to some of your tasty drinks, Diona!

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: ...It's a deal! Next time you're in Mondstadt, I'll treat you to the best drinks you've ever tasted — the kind with absolutely zippo alcohol!

response.speaker: Barbeloth
response.text: By the way, if you have any more questions about your card, look for someone named Mona. You probably already know who I'm talking about?

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: Mona? Yeah, I know her! She always orders the cheapest drinks. Is she a powerful fortune teller, too?

response.speaker: Barbeloth
response.text: Hah, she's nowhere near my level. Still, she should be up to the task of reading the Lunar Arcana — otherwise, she might as well hang up her hat.

response.speaker: Barbeloth
response.text: Just tell her you've brought a prophecy on behalf of the Mighty Astromancer Barbeloth Trismegistus — as a test.

response.speaker: Barbeloth
response.text: Don't worry. As long as you say that, she'll do her best to interpret it for you.

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: Mmhmm, I think I got that! Astro... mancer... Barbeloth Trismegistus... Meows, that's a long name...

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: Come to think of it, isn't Mona's name really long, too? I think it was... the Astrolo... What was it again?

choices.text: If you ever need help, just let me know.
But given everything we know about Diona's motivations...
Just relax and draw a card.
Where did you run into him?
What are you doing in Fontaine?
How else could I handle so many commissions?
